message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the **federal statutory holidays** that create long‑weekend breaks in Canada during 2023, along with the exact dates of the holiday and the full weekend stretch that people usually enjoy:

| Holiday | Date in 2023 | Long‑Weekend Period (Friday – Sunday) |
|---------|--------------|--------------------------------------|
| **Family Day** (most provinces) | **February 20** (Monday) | **Feb 18 – 20** (Fri – Sun) |
| **Good Friday** | **April 7** (Friday) | **Apr 7 – 9** (Fri – Sun) |
| **Victoria Day** | **May 22** (Monday) | **May 20 – 22** (Fri – Sun) |
| **Canada Day** | **July 1** (Saturday) – *Observed* **July 3** (Monday) | **Jul 1 – 3** (Sat – Mon) |
| **Labour Day** | **September 4** (Monday) | **Sep 2 – 4** (Fri – Sun) |
| **Thanksgiving** | **October 9** (Monday) | **Oct 7 – 9** (Fri – Sun) |
| **Christmas Day** | **December 25** (Monday) | **Dec 23 – 25** (Fri – Mon) |

> **Quick notes**  
> • New Year’s Day 2023 fell on Sunday, so the holiday was observed on Monday **Dec 31 2022**, giving a long weekend **Dec 30 – 31 2022** (outside the 2023 calendar).  
> • Remembrance Day (Thu Nov 11) and Boxing Day (Tue Dec 26) did not produce a traditional long weekend in 2023.

Feel free to plug these dates straight into your holiday‑planning app! If you’d like provincial‑specific holidays (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Ontario, St. George’s Day in BC, etc.) let me know and I can add those too.
